message.content:
I read Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024‑09‑28, filed 2024‑11‑01), the morning feed, and the news, then bought.

**What I found:** Apple's FY2024 total net sales were **$391,035M** (+2% y/y), operating income **$123,216M**, net income **$93,736M**, and diluted EPS **$6.08** — with net income dragged down by the one‑time **$10.2B** net State Aid tax charge (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%); excluding that item the underlying business actually improved, with gross margin up to 46.2% on Services strength ($96,169M, +13%). Cash generation remains exceptional at **$118,254M** operating cash flow, against $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. The Q4 release (31 Oct) showed quarterly revenue of $94.9B, +6% y/y — the first solid growth quarter in a year. The feed showed AAPL drifting mildly lower through the first half‑hour (≈221.8 → ≈220.5) on no news of substance — headlines were only "shares little changed," "iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December," and "analysts keep holiday‑quarter estimates unchanged" — and the latest quote was $222.70 (bid 222.68 / ask 222.72). That is a steady, fairly valued large cap with improving margins and no adverse catalyst today, so I executed one buy rather than standing aside.

**Order:** Bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00** (≈0.1% above the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask), filled in full at $223.00 for a total of **$9,812** — within the $10,000 per‑order cap, the $20,000 daily cap (no other orders today), and leaving the account's $50,000 cash comfortably intact with no withdrawal. Position after trade: 100 MSFT shares + 44 AAPL shares.

*Caveat worth flagging:* the fill came at the top of my limit ($0.30 above the quote I sized off), and the feed's last prints (≈220.5) were modestly below the quote timestamp, so intraday price is noisy — a resting limit near the touch was the right tool, but a limit at $223.25–223.50 would have given slightly more fill certainty had price kept drifting up.
message.reasoning_content:
Filled at 223.0 — that's exactly the limit; price presumably rose slightly. 44 × 223 = $9,812, under $10,000. Total today $9,812 ≤ $20,000. No money moved out.

Note: fill at limit price 223 vs market 222.70 — slight slippage of $0.30 (~0.13%), acceptable.
